newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Ex-Im bank to extend loan to Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Japan Ex-Im bank to extend loan to Argentina.

text.p: The Export-Import Bank of Japan said on Tuesday that it would extend and guarantee loans to Argentina in a credit agreement worth about 18.5 billion yen.
The proceeds will be used to help prevent flood damage and develop transportation networks in the seven northern states of Argentina, the Ex-Im Bank said in a statement.

It said it would provide 12.9 billion yen to Argentina, equivalent to 70 percent of the total amount, while the remaining 5.5 billion yen would be co-financed by seven commercial banks, led by Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi.
The Ex-Im Bank will also provide guarantees for the credit extended by the commercial banks.
The loan is part of a co-financing arrangement with the World Bank. The World Bank plans to extend credit totalling $200 million to Argentina for this project.
